text:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: Auto-detected spike in control-plane errors from Azure westeurope region for Private deployments. Alerting SRE on-call. Patterns: DNS NXDOMAIN + TCP retransmits to control-plane endpoints.

Maria Chen: seeing 504/502 for Private control-plane heartbeats since ~08:03 UTC. Affected: customers with ExpressRoute / VPNs terminating in westeurope. On-prem connector tunnels dropping.

Akash Patel: looking now. Observability shows a sudden rise in TCP retransmits to 35.198.x.x and 35.199.x.x (our control-plane egress). Azure NVA telemetry shows route flap for our peered prefixes and Azure DNS returning SERVFAIL for redwood-priv.internal in some AZs.

Diane O'Connor: CS has 4 high-priority tickets: two enterprise customers report connector flaps and one reports API 401s during reconnect storms. Customers asking if data plane is impacted.

Maria Chen: tagging @eng-oncall @sre-bot. Setting severity=P1 due to multiple enterprise impacts and on-prem tunnels failing.

sre-bot: Incident record created: INC-2026-0421-12, severity=P1, responders=[Maria Chen, Akash Patel]. Paging on-call now.

Akash Patel: opened support case with Azure Networking; initial reply: they see a partial fabric fault affecting certain subnets in westeurope and are investigating. Also requesting Azure DNS team to check recursive resolver errors for our private zone.

Maria Chen: mitigation plan brainstorm: (A) failover affected Private control-plane endpoints to our eu-north1 control-plane and rotate DNS, (B) push static fallback IPs to customer connectors (requires allowlist updates), (C) temporary GRE tunnel through eu-west2 relay nodes to bypass Azure fabric.

Luis Gomez: note: two customers have strict allowlists and cannot quickly accept new IPs. Need Ops to prep signed allowlist updates. CS to coordinate with their security teams.

Akash Patel: started capture on relay nodes and on-prem connectors. Observed TLS handshake stalls before the server cert arrives — packet drops on initial TCP 3-way in certain Azure leafs.

eng-oncall: deployed short TTL change for redwood-priv.internal (TTL=20) and added fallback A records pointing to eu-north1 for control-plane. Pushing config now.

Maria Chen: posting customer-facing message draft in #support-bridge: "We are investigating intermittent connectivity from Azure westeurope to Redwood Private control-plane. Engineers are working with Azure and have deployed temporary routing/DNS mitigations. We'll update within 15 minutes."

Diane O'Connor: sent message to affected customers and invited them to private incident channel. One enterprise asked for timeline for failover — told them canary in ~10 mins.

Akash Patel: Azure confirms fabric fix attempt scheduled; in parallel we are standing up GRE tunnel from relays in westeurope to eu-north1 to ferry control-plane traffic for affected customers. Rolling canary for 3 customers.

Maria Chen: canary started. Monitoring auth, latencies, and reconnects.

eng-oncall: canary metrics look promising after 4 minutes: error-rate down from 42% -> 8% for canary customers. Proceeding to staged rollout in 3 waves.

sre-bot: Action recorded: TTL reduced to 20s; fallback A records added; GRE tunnels established for 3 relay instances. Auto-rollback disabled for these actions.

Akash Patel: collecting tcpdump from on-prem site that still sees packet loss — noticed ICMP unreachable messages coming from Azure gateway before the fabric fix window. Sending logs to Azure support and requesting route stability confirmation.

Luis Gomez: CS update 6: enterprise allowlist updates underway; one customer completed allowlist change and is on failover path.

Diane O'Connor: customer comms updated: "Mitigation in place: we have partial failover to alternate control-plane region and GRE tunnels for affected relays. Azure is applying a fix to their fabric. We're monitoring and will follow up with a full RCA." :information_source:

eng-oncall: staged rollout to remaining affected customers complete. Most customers show steady state. Two still experiencing intermittent TLS handshake timeouts.

Akash Patel: Azure reports they cleared a spine/leaf fault at 08:29 UTC and purged affected DNS caches. They expect residual issues to clear within TTL windows.

Maria Chen: preparing handoff to night shift @Akash Patel for monitoring and post-incident tasks. I'll draft timeline and start RCA doc.

sre-bot: Handoff recorded  from Maria Chen to Akash Patel at 08:45 UTC. Incident status: monitoring. Last observed error-rate: 6%.

Akash Patel: taking handoff. Current mitigations remain: TTL low for 60 minutes, fallback A records active, GRE tunnels will be torn down once Azure confirms stability for 1 hour. Plan: revert GRE, restore TTL to normal, and publish mitigation timeline.

Luis Gomez: confirmed all enterprise allowlist updates processed except one customer whose firewall vendor needs a vendor-signed IP block. CS to coordinate.

Diane O'Connor: posted final customer update to incident channel: "Service largely restored; mitigations applied. For customers still impacted, we are working directly to complete allowlist updates or coordinate alternative routing."

Maria Chen: postmortem owners assigned: Akash (network root cause), Diane (customer comms), Maria (timelines and mitigation playbook). Target: preliminary RCA within 24 hours. :memo:

sre-bot: Incident INC-2026-0421-12 moved to postmortemPending. Pager closed for current on-call. Reopen threshold: error-rate > 10% OR any enterprise connector still failing.

eng-oncall: follow-ups added to backlog: (1) automate cross-region failover for Private connectors, (2) test GRE relay flow in DR playbook, (3) verify Azure DNS private zone monitoring and RCODE anomaly alerts.

Akash Patel: pasting mitigation commands for runbook reference:

```
# Reduce Azure DNS TTL (example az cli)
az network dns record-set a update --resource-group rg-dns --zone-name redwood-priv.internal --name control --set ttl=20
# Create fallback A record
az network dns record-set a add-record --resource-group rg-dns --zone-name redwood-priv.internal --record-set-name control --ipv4-address <eu-north1-ip>

# GRE tunnel example (on relay)
sudo ip link add gre1 type gretap local <relay-egress> remote <eu-north1-relay>
sudo ip link set gre1 up
sudo ip route add <control-plane-ip>/32 dev gre1

# tcpdump to capture TLS handshake issues
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 tcp port 443 and host <control-plane-ip> -w /tmp/handshake.pcap
```

Maria Chen: thank you team. I'll circulate the incident timeline and schedule the postmortem. :heart:
